name: Rangeland & Land Use

objectives.text: Sort pictures of land into uses such as farmland, pasture, rangeland, forest, and town
Identify livestock commonly raised on pasture and rangeland such as beef cattle, sheep, and goats
Describe how grazing animals use grassland and rangeland for food
Identify products and benefits people receive from rangeland such as meat, wool, wildlife habitat, clean water, and recreation
Classify common range plants as grasses, grass-likes, forbs, or shrubs using their visible features
Compare how a rotational grazing system and a continuous grazing system affect the health of a pasture
Explain why some range plants are valued as desirable forage while others are classed as undesirable, poisonous, or invasive
Calculate a stocking rate for a pasture using forage production, animal units, and animal unit months
Explain how overgrazing changes rangeland plant cover and increases the risk of erosion
Describe how land capability classes rate land for cropping, grazing, woodland, or other uses
Describe the characteristics of rangeland and the global importance of the rangeland biome in providing ecosystem services
Describe the environmental effects of livestock grazing on rangeland including impacts on soil, plant communities, water quality, and carbon storage
Describe careers in range management and land-use planning such as range conservationist, land manager, and rancher and the role they play in the economy
Determine the range condition of a site by comparing its current plant species composition with its ecological site potential
Apply rangeland management practices such as prescribed burning, brush control, water development, and cross fencing to improve grazing distribution and range health
Develop a grazing plan for a supervised agricultural experience livestock enterprise that includes stocking rate, rotation schedule, and forage monitoring
Analyze how a region's land-use pattern of farmland, rangeland, forest, and development affects its natural resources
Assess how conversion of rangeland to cropland, urban development, and energy extraction affects the availability of rangeland resources
Evaluate the plant and animal biodiversity of a rangeland site and recommend practices that enhance its ecosystem function
Compare how private ownership, federal grazing permits, and conservation easements shape decisions about rangeland use
Revise a rangeland management plan so that it supports livestock production, wildlife habitat, water supply, and other ecosystem services together
Design a master land-use plan for a given area that uses land capability classes to assign cropland, rangeland, and development
Evaluate a land-use decision by weighing economic needs against the responsibility to conserve soil, water, and wildlife for future generations

changes: Removed the invalid code FPS.04.01.04.b and used only candidate codes. Kept all six original objectives, adding rangeland to the grade 2 sort. Added objectives on range livestock, rangeland products, range plant classification, forage desirability, stocking rate and animal unit months, land capability classes, rangeland characteristics and ecosystem services, grazing environmental effects, range careers, range condition assessment, range improvement practices, an SAE grazing plan, rangeland conversion, biodiversity evaluation, ownership and permits, plan revision, and master land-use design. Erosion control, forestry, and wildlife management detail were left to the sibling sub-topics.
